evidence_notes: Claim: Venus is unlikely to be livable and sending people is too risky; support is source facts (97% carbon dioxide, corrosive sulfuric acid clouds, heat) plus a stray para on NASA/orbits that does not bear on the claim. org 3 (controlling idea buried mid-essay, one part digresses, opening does not orient); dev 3 (specific figures but source phrasing lightly stitched -- patchwritten -- and support listed); conv 3 (duplications 'acid in acid in', 'Also whats possibly on Also whats possibly on', errors accumulate, reader re-reads to repair but never guesses); arg 4 (one reason reasoned -- lethal atmosphere/heat would 'wipe everything off the planet' -- no opposing view, no qualification)

Claim: 'This is right' -- the emotion-reading technology is good -- but the referent is never named; support is the 83/9/6/2 percentage list and a marked quote from Dr. Huang with a works cited; second half is an unsupported utopian chain (no violence, world peace). org 2 (begins mid-argument with no antecedent, controlling idea only inferable from the body, no functioning opening); dev 3 (percentages specific but listed, the utopian claims wholly unsupported); conv 3 (gald, workd, xepress, pefrom, beacuse -- errors accumulate, reader re-reads to repair); arg 3 (position committed but reasons asserted, the smiles-to-world-peace chain is a leap, no why on the page)

Claim: self-driving cars are a good idea, stated in sentence one and held; support is the drunk-driver scenario (realized and explained), the cost of better roads, manufacturer profits, and a liability question raised from the text. org 3 (para on roads/profits/hovercraft digresses and the unit carries several jobs, unity breaks); dev 4 (drunk-driving example specific and its connection to safety stated, but most other support general and asserted); conv 3 (no capitalization, wreacks/wreaks, 'the the car', 'beheld responcibale' -- errors accumulate, reader re-reads); arg 4 (safety reason genuinely reasoned; liability/laws mentioned but never answered, so rung 5 fails)

Claim (in Luke Bomberger's voice): join the UNRRA as a Seagoing Cowboy, because you help the devastated and see the world; support is named landmarks -- Acropolis, gondola in Venice, excavated castle in Crete, Panama Canal -- and an empathy appeal. org 4 (idea stated early, frame present, but the helping part and the sightseeing part could swap without loss); dev 4 (landmarks specific and tied to the call to join, but the helping-others support is general, so not specific throughout); conv 4 (devestated, expirience x3, appriciative visible throughout but nothing needs repair; sentences vary -- questions, imperatives); arg 4 (reciprocity reason reasoned -- imagine being devastated and wanting help -- but conclusion is what the prompt already implies)

Claim: the facial action coding system would help teachers reach struggling students; support is two marked quotes from D'Alto/Dr. Huang plus reasoning about alternative assignments and students who never ask for help. org 4 (idea stated at end of intro and held, all parts relate, but the online-homework stretch wanders and does not return); dev 4 (quotes specific and marked, connection stated -- 'This shows that...' -- but by restatement, and para 4's claims are general); conv 3 ('By being said the students that can't comprehend the lesson, there can be an alternative assignment that they can to so' -- reader re-reads to repair; indivuals, mordern, diffucult, insturctor accumulate); arg 4 (the why is reasoned -- students skip or copy rather than ask, so unnoticed confusion compounds -- no opposing view, conclusion the prompt implies)

No position on whether studying Venus is worthy -- only 'is a informative text' and a closing 'the scientuifics lookk Venus interesting'; body is three signposted fact-clusters (heat/pressure, orbital observation limits, silicon electronics and WWII) with no idea binding them. org 2 (parts do different jobs but no controlling idea is stated -- the reader must assemble it, and the 'Lastly' part has no recoverable relation to the rest); dev 3 (800 degrees and 90x pressure are specific but source phrasing is stitched in near-verbatim -- patchwriting caps at 3 -- and support is listed, never explained); conv 2 (the 'Lastly' paragraph is unrecoverable -- 'this things starts doo do about 1800's' -- reader must guess, meaning somewhat obscured, though paras 1-2 parse); arg 2 (position is the near-empty 'informative text / scientists find it interesting' -- so limited it barely engages the issue, no commitment added)

Claim: limiting car usage brings advantages -- less pollution, more activity, saved money; support is marked quotes with figures (12 percent and up to 50 percent emissions, Vauban's 5,500 residents, Bogota's 118 miles of bike paths) each followed by the writer's comment. org 4 (idea stated early and held with a real frame, but the Vauban cluster and the Bogota cluster are parallel and could swap without loss); dev 4 (figures specific and connection explicitly stated -- 'This meaning...', 'you can conclude...' -- but the explanations mostly restate the quote rather than interpret it); conv 4 ('there is advantages', 'store are placed', 'have been replaces', respondible, bicylce are visible but nothing needs repair; sentences vary but errors are past occasional); arg 4 (walkable-suburb reason reasoned -- destinations within walking distance means no gas spent -- no opposing view, conclusion the prompt implies)

Opening states both 'exploring Venus is not a great idea' and 'Studying Venus is a worthy [pursuit]'; the body then argues Venus is unsafe while the final paragraph reports feasibility facts (170 degrees, sea-level air pressure) that sit under neither, and the essay ends mid-quote. org 2 (controlling idea contradicted in its own opening, no closing -- text stops inside a quotation, final part unrelated to the stated position); dev 2 (borrowed material stands in for the argument -- long verbatim source stretches, mostly unmarked, with only 'This shows that Venus is not a safe planet' as the writer's own connective work); conv 3 ('Studying Venus is a worthy because it's closes to our planet to earth', 'The scientists are been send' -- reader re-reads to repair, meaning stays recoverable); arg 2 (the prompt's own wording handed back in sentence two with no commitment added, and immediately contradicted -- rung 3 fails on commitment)

Claim: using emotion-reading technology in classrooms is valuable, stated in a one-sentence thesis with three previewed reasons and held throughout; support is the article's tailored-lesson mechanism plus realized scenarios (FACS notifies someone or tells a stressed student to take a break). org 4 (idea stated early, frame present, all parts relate, but the three bodies mirror the previewed list and could swap freely); dev 4 (mechanism particulars specific and their connection stated with added reasoning -- students don't self-advocate -- but 'a lot of students' / 'many students' claims are general, so not specific throughout); conv 4 (acknowleding, attendence, 'each students needs', a comma splice and a faulty parallel -- visible but nothing needs repair; control slips only on the longer sentences); arg 4 (reason reasoned -- students who hide confusion never get help, so a system that detects it changes the outcome -- no opposing view such as privacy, conclusion the prompt implies)

Verdict, given only at the end: the author supported his idea that studying Venus is worthy despite the dangers; para 1 paraphrases the dangers into the writer's own words (97% carbon dioxide, 800 degrees, 90x pressure), para 2 lists three marked quotes as the author's reasons. org 3 (controlling idea weakly located -- surfaces mid-essay and is fully stated only in the closing; the opening reports facts without orienting); dev 4 (figures and quotes specific and framed as the author's reasons, but each after-quote sentence restates rather than interprets); conv 4 (Althrough, fetures, 'ans craters', 'the temperatures average is', a sentence break after the subordinator -- visible, never needing repair; word choice sometimes approximate); arg 3 (verdict is the prompt's wording handed back and affirmed; the essay never says why those reasons make the case well -- asserted, not shown, and it circles its position)
